summary: Philip Whalen was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned his BA at Reed College (~1946–1951) and studied under Richard Baker in 1972. He served as abbot at Hartford Street Zen Center (1991) and resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo (~1984–1987).

Philipp André Maas earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Bonn (1997–2004) under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. His posts in Indology and philosophy include assistant professor at the University of Vienna (2010–2016) and Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the University of Leipzig (2016–2026).

Philipp Keiper, an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1873–1877), studying under Friedrich von Spiegel. He later taught at Gymnasium Fridericianum Erlangen (~1881–1890) and Theodor-Heuss-Gymnasium Ludwigshafen (~1890–1920).
Philipp Schäffer was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Max Walleser and completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University between 1920 and 1924.

Philippe Colinet was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at KU Leuven (1881–1884) under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He also studied under Johannes Schmidt, Michel Bréal, and Abel Bergaigne before becoming a professor at KU Leuven (1887, 1889).

Philippe Stern studied history, archaeology, and Indology under Louis Finot (~1921–1927). He served as professor of Indian art and archaeology at the École du Louvre (1929–1965) and as Conservateur-en-chef at the Guimet Museum (1954–1965).

Philippe Turenne is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2010) under G. Victor Sōgen Hori. He also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and with Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche.

Philippe Édouard Foucaux specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Eugène Burnouf in 1838. He held professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1842, 1854), the Collège de France (1857, 1870–1894), and the University of Paris (~1862–1894).
Phillip Bloom is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology who earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.

Philoxène Luzzatto worked in Indology and linguistics and studied under Samuel David Luzzatto. He was a member of the Accademia Galileiana (~1851–1854) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1852–1854).
Phra Athiwat Thammawatsiri earned a Ph.D. in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and later served there as a lecturer and researcher in the field of Buddhist studies.

Phra Brahmapundit is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as Buddhist Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996) and Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018). He also led the International Council for the Day of Vesak (~2004–2018).

Phra Rajavaramuni is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a B.A. from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and a B.A. from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University. He was Dean of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Bachelor of Liberal Arts at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an M.A. in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Phramaha Niras Ruangsan specialized in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a Master's (-2009) and a PhD (-2015) at the University of Sydney under Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan, before receiving a doctorate at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (2017).

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) under supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, having also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (2015) and as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center (2015).

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a B.A. from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA from the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff earned her Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1969–1973) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. A scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, she was a professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and later served at Yale University (2004).
Pia Guerrini Bione was an Indology scholar who completed her Dr.phil. at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa (1903–1907), having also studied in its Classe di Lettere e Filosofia during those years.
